newsitem.title: UK: C&G sees 1997 mortgage margins widen.
newsitem.headline: C&G sees 1997 mortgage margins widen.

text.p: Cheltenham & Gloucester Plc, the UK building society that was taken over by the Lloyds TSB Group in 1995, said on Thursday that margins in 1997 were tending to widen after cut-throat competition in the home loans market.

The C&G said that in the absence of a buoyant house buying market, competition for remortgage business over the last couple of years had been fierce and some customer offers were thus "clearly unsustainable in the longer run".
"We are already seeing a return to a more healthy situation and while competition will continue to be keen, margins in 1997 are tending to widen," said chairman-designate Andrew Longhurst.

The C&G earlier posted a hefty 36 percent rise in annual pretax profits to 336 million pounds in comparison to pro forma figures for 1995. Mortgage assets at the year-end were up 10.7 percent at 28.36 billion, it noted.
Gross mortgage lending had risen 92 percent to 6.74 billion and the group now has a 15.1 percent share of UK net mortgage lending.
"With C&G mortgages becoming available this year also through all branches of TSB, the group is well positioned to benefit from an improving housing market," Longhurst said.

In the first full year in which C&G mortgages were sold also through Lloyds Bank branches, gross new mortgage lending reached 6.74 billion pounds, of which 3.6 billion was generated through C&G's 230 branches alone.
This compares with gross lending of 3.51 billion pounds in 1995 when the distribution network was still developing.

Since December, the C&G no longer promises to undercut the average variable base mortgage rate paid by existing borrowers of its main five rivals. "From February 1997, C&G once again has total flexibility in the setting of its mortgage interest rate, and the timing of any change," it stated.

As the house-purchase mortgage market started to revive in the latter half of the year, C&G said the nature of competition changed with the major lenders easing back on the aggressive new borrower incentives offered in a chase for remortgage customers. C&G's total capital ratio at the year-end was 10.3 percent, compared with 9.9 percent at year-end 1995, and the tier 1 ratio stood at 7.9 percent, compared with 8.1 percent previously.
